title: DKA 3 of 7, step-down / telemetry: type 1 diabetes in DKA after months of cost-related insulin rationing (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
diagnosis: Diabetic ketoacidosis with severe biochemical features (glucose 684, pH 7.23, bicarbonate 9, anion gap 27, BHB 7.2) in type 1 diabetes after 3 months of stretching insulin she could not afford; prerenal AKI; low potassium (3.2) with insulin held on Day 1 morning and replaced by peripheral piggybacks; low phosphate monitored; low glucose after a fixed meal dose with a small lunch; discharge with medicines and supplies in hand
desc: Mon 11/09 0700 to Thu 11/12 0700. A 38-year-old single mother who lost her insurance and rationed insulin arrives in DKA; care ends with medicines and supplies in hand. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.
